research_questions.statement: Can deep operator networks (DeepONets) learn nonlinear operators accurately and efficiently from relatively small datasets?

provenance.text_excerpt: Therefore, unstacked DeepONets with bias achieve the best performance.

claims.statement: Unstacked DeepONets with bias achieve the best performance among tested DeepONet variants.

provenance.text_excerpt: We perform systematic simulations for identifying two types of operators, i.e., dynamic systems and partial differential equations, and demonstrate that DeepONet significantly reduces the generalization error compared to the fully-connected networks.

claims.statement: DeepONets significantly reduce generalization error compared to fully-connected networks.

datasets.description: Synthetic dataset for learning the antiderivative operator. Input functions u are sampled from a Gaussian random field with length scale 0.2, evaluated at 100 fixed sensors. Output functions are the antiderivative evaluated at random y points. Training set size 10000, test set size 100000.
datasets.name: Antiderivative operator dataset

experiments_or_tasks: Comparing stacked and unstacked DeepONets with and without bias against fully-connected neural networks (FNNs) as baseline.

Learning the antiderivative operator G: u(x) -> s(x) = integral_0^x u(tau) dtau, with input functions u sampled from a Gaussian random field (GRF) with length scale l=0.2, using 100 sensors, 10000 training points, 100000 test points, and 50000 iterations.

methods.name: DeepONet (stacked and unstacked)
methods.protocol_description: DeepONet consists of a trunk network taking y as input and outputting [t1,...,tp], and branch network(s) taking [u(x1),...,u(xm)] as input and outputting [b1,...,bp]. The output is sum_{k=1}^p b_k t_k, optionally with bias b0. Stacked DeepONet uses p separate branch networks; unstacked DeepONet uses a single branch network outputting a vector. Trunk depth 3, width 40; branch depth 2, width 40. Activation functions applied in last layer of trunk. Trained with Adam optimizer for 50000 iterations.

methods.name: Fully-connected neural network (FNN) baseline
methods.protocol_description: FNN takes concatenated input [u(x1),...,u(xm), y] and outputs G(u)(y). Hyperparameters grid searched: depth 2-4, width 10-2560, learning rate 0.0001-0.01. Best performance: depth 2, width 2560, learning rate 0.001.

study_units.name: DeepONet architecture and baseline comparison

provenance.text_excerpt: Among all these hyperparameters, the smallest test error ∼10−4 is obtained for the network with depth 2, width 2560, and learning rate 0.001.

results.metric_name: Test error comparison: unstacked vs stacked

provenance.text_excerpt: Compared to stacked DeepONets, although unstacked DeepONets have larger training error, the test error is smaller, due to the smaller generalization error.

results.value_raw_text: unstacked DeepONets have larger training error, the test error is smaller, due to the smaller generalization error

provenance.text_excerpt: The training trajectory of an unstacked DeepONet with bias is shown in Fig. 3A, and the generalization error is negligible.

We observe that for both stacked and unstacked DeepONets, adding bias to branch networks and Eq. (2) reduces both training and test errors (Fig. 3B); DeepONets with bias also have smaller uncertainty, i.e., more stable for training from random initialization (Fig. 3B).

results.value_raw_text: adding bias to branch networks and Eq. (2) reduces both training and test errors
